questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Two prepositions with one verb
questions.learningObjective: Use two prepositions with one verb

stimulus.body: The projection note says the legend refers to the symbols. The writer chooses the verb with two prepositions.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly uses a verb with two prepositions?

options.text: Die Legende bezieht sich mit die Symbole
Die Legende bezieht sich auf die Symbole
Die Legende bezieht sich an die Symbole
Die Legende bezieht sich auf den Symbole

questions.explanation: sich beziehen binds auf plus accusative, so auf die Symbole is correct; replacing or changing the preposition or case breaks the collocation.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The preposition of a verb of opinion
questions.learningObjective: Use the preposition of a verb of opinion
questions.stem: Stage one: the note says the reviewer likes the design. Stage two: choose the verb of opinion.

options.text: Der Reviewer haelt fuer das Design
Der Reviewer haelt ueber das Design
Der Reviewer haelt von dem Design
Der Reviewer haelt von das Design

questions.explanation: halten von expresses an opinion and governs the dative, so von dem Design is correct; changing the preposition or case breaks the collocation.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: An article that changes the meaning of a working day
questions.learningObjective: Use an article that changes meaning of a working day
questions.stem: The note writes am Freitag. Why is am used here?

options.text: am is a definite article
am is the contraction of an den
am is an independent preposition
am is the contraction of an dem

questions.explanation: am contracts an dem, so am Freitag is correct; treating it as an accusative contraction, an independent preposition, or an article is wrong.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The participle as a predicate after sein
questions.learningObjective: Use a participle as predicate after sein
questions.stem: Explain why the note writes die Karte ist gedruckt and not die Karte ist drucken.

answer.exemplar: sein plus a past participle forms a state, so gedruckt is correct; drucken is an infinitive and cannot serve as the participle predicate.

questions.explanation: sein governs a past participle to express a state, so gedruckt is required; using the infinitive drucken breaks the construction.
questions.hint: sein plus past participle forms a state.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The state passive and the process passive
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish state passive from process passive

stimulus.body: The projection note says the border is closed. The writer chooses the passive form that expresses a state.

questions.stem: Which passive form expresses a state?

options.text: Die Grenze wird geschlossen expresses a process
Die Grenze ist geschlossen expresses a state
Die Grenze hat geschlossen is wrong tense
Die Grenze war geschlossen werden is ungrammatical

questions.explanation: sein plus past participle expresses a state, so ist geschlossen is a state; wird geschlossen is a process, and wrong auxiliaries are errors.
questions.hint: sein passive is state, werden passive is process.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The adjective after a possessive in the dative
questions.learningObjective: Use adjective after possessive in dative
questions.stem: Stage one: the note writes meinem alten Freund. Stage two: choose the adjective ending.

options.text: meinem alten Freundes uses genitive ending
meinem alten Freunde adds an extra e
meinem alten Freund uses strong ending
meinem alten Freunden uses plural ending

questions.explanation: A dative possessive is weakly declined, so the adjective takes a strong ending without an extra e; genitive, plural, or extra-e forms are errors.
questions.hint: Dative possessive takes strong adjective ending.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The adjective after a linking verb
questions.learningObjective: Use adjective after a linking verb
questions.stem: The note writes die Karte scheint genau. Why is genau uninflected?

options.text: genau takes no ending after sein
options.misconception: confuses with sein instead of scheinen

options.text: scheinen is a transitive verb
genau is an adverb here
scheinen is a linking verb

questions.explanation: scheinen is a linking verb, so the adjective stays uninflected; calling it transitive, an adverb, or confusing it with sein misrepresents the construction.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Two prepositions with one verb
questions.learningObjective: Use two prepositions with one verb
questions.stem: Explain why the note writes die Karte haengt von dem Massstab ab and not die Karte haengt mit dem Massstab ab.

answer.exemplar: abhaengen binds von plus dative, so von dem Massstab is correct; mit would replace the bound preposition and break the collocation.

questions.explanation: abhaengen governs von, so von dem Massstab is required; using mit would misreplace the bound preposition and produce an ungrammatical collocation.

options.text: der Montag is a different construction
